about.title: Bradbury Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Bradbury is a small place. With roughly 1,089 residents spread across quiet hillside streets like Mount Olive Drive, Woodlyn Lane, Gardi Street and Bradbury Hills Road, most neighbors know one another, and a sudden death is felt by the whole community. In 2024, the city's final public-record count showed zero traffic deaths within its limits. That is worth noting, yet wrongful death claims involving Bradbury families still arise—often from a collision elsewhere in Los Angeles County, a medical error, an unsafe property, or a workplace incident. When someone else's negligence causes a death, California law lets a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children bring a civil claim first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and shorter when a public agency is involved. We handle these cases directly, on contingency, so you can focus on grieving while our team handles the paperwork.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death claim—spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. Our team can sort out standing early, before anything else is decided.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity is involved. Getting our team involved promptly protects that timeline.

items.title: No cost to you, ever
items.desc: We take wrongful death cases on contingency—no fee unless there is a recovery. Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance.

items.question: Bradbury recorded no traffic deaths in 2024. Can a wrongful death claim still involve our family?
items.answer: Yes. A claim follows the family, not the city line, so a Bradbury resident who died in a crash on a freeway across Los Angeles County, in a hospital, or on someone else's property may still have a case. The local numbers are neutral public-record counts and do not limit anyone's rights. Our team can look at where and how the death occurred and explain what applies.

items.question: The other driver is being prosecuted. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and runs separately from any criminal case, with a different standard of proof and a different goal. Families do not need a conviction to move forward, and waiting can put the two-year deadline at risk. Speaking with our team early keeps both tracks in view.

items.question: What does a wrongful death claim actually cover in California?
items.answer: California law allows recovery of funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. The exact picture depends on the family's circumstances and the facts of the death. No one can promise a result, but our team can walk you through what the law recognizes in your situation.
